Reasoning Models02

Reasoning Effort

Clearly, reasoning effort has some effect on the model's abilities and also on the cost to run the model

Reasoning Models03

Asking irishQwen a word problem

irishQwen immediately answers with 16,  the first number in the question. How can we get irishQwen to respond with better answers?

◆ GSM8K — 8.5K grade-school math word problems written by people (Cobbe et al., 2021), 2 to 8 steps of + − × ÷ each, the answer one number. We used 100 from its test set, Janet’s ducks is one of them.

Reasoning Models · One Pass per Token04

Zero-Shot Chain of Thought (Kojima et al., 2022)

One technique is to just ask the model to think more

text-davinci-002just answer"Let's think step by step."
MultiArith17.7%78.7%
GSM8K10.4%40.7%

Same model, same weights, a different prompt.  This works inordinately well for how stupid it is.

◆ Chain of thought — the intermediate steps, written out as tokens before the answer.

Reasoning Models · One Pass per Token05

Forward Pass as Context

◆ Forward pass — one trip through all 28 blocks: the model's whole budget for one token.

We could think of multiple forward passes as increasing the context the model has available to it.

Reasoning Models · One Pass per Token06

Why Chain of Thought Works

Every token it writes goes back in as input. 250 tokens of steps is 250 more forward passes, and the 9 it wrote down is sitting in the context when it gets to 9 × 2.

Reasoning Models · One Pass per Token07

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

Last class we looked at improving a model's answer by giving more context in the input prompt.

We did this by augmenting the user's prompt with information retrieved from an external database. (Hence retrieval augmented generation)

Reasoning Models · One Pass per Token08

Language Models are Few‑Shot Learners (Brown et al., 2020)

This introduced the idea of in-context learning: show GPT-3 a few examples in the prompt and it does the task.

◆ In-context learning — "learning" a task from examples in the prompt, without changing a single weight.

Reasoning Models · Asking for Steps09

Few-shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting (Wei et al., 2022)

◆ Chain-of-thought prompting — few-shot examples that show their steps, so the model shows its steps.

Few-shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting is downstream of "in-context learning"

Reasoning Models · Asking for Steps10

Chain-of-Thought Prompting Needs Scale

If we put a few worked examples in the prompt, with their steps written out, the model writes steps too.

GSM8Kexamples with just answersexamples with the steps
GPT-3 (175B)15.6%46.9%
PaLM (540B)17.9%56.9%

Note: Results using irishQwen with CoT Prompting on GSM8K

Reasoning Models · Asking for Steps11

Chain of Thought Sampling

For a harder problem, Toula's pastries (3 × 68 + 2 × 80 + 6 × 55 = 694). We can ask 8 times, keeping the answer that comes up most:

Wrong answers tend to be wrong in different ways.

◆ Self-consistency — sample several chains of thought, majority vote on the final answer (Wang et al., 2022: PaLM GSM8K 56.5% → 74.4% with 40 samples).

Note: irishQwen with one sample: 64%, irishQwen sampling 8 CoTs: 76%

Reasoning Models · Asking for Steps12

Prompt Engineering Sucks

How do we teach the model to think automatically?

DeepSeek-R1-Zero was trained using reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards and taught itself to "think"

◆ Verifiable reward — a checker: 1 for right, 0 for wrong.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner13

DeepSeek-R1-Zero

Reinforcement Learning directly, no SFT at all. The prompt asks it to reason inside think tags: <think>...</think>, then answer.

This boils down to asking the model to fill its own context before answering and rewarding it when it does.

This is all "thinking" in LLMs is.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner14

DeepSeek-R1-Zero

R1-Zero didn't see a single chain of thought during training but after thousands of RL steps (DeepSeek-AI, 2025):

AIME 2024startend of RLmajority vote
DeepSeek-R1-Zero15.6%71.0%86.7%

Its answers got longer and longer on their own: more thinking earned more reward. Partway through training the model started stopping to re-check its own work ("Wait, …") and trying another approach.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner15

Interpretability - Chain of Thoughts

A downside of RLing CoTs: chains of thought can be hard to read, and DeepSeek-R1-Zero mixed languages mid-thought.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner16

Astra Thinking Traces - Think like a caveman

<thinking>
Oops typo "stylesheet" accidental. Need avoid. We already send? We need final proper. Since not yet sent. Ask clean.
</thinking>

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner17

DeepSeek-R1

Using the thinking traces that DeepSeek-R1-Zero learned, we can teach smaller models how to think by distilling on the thinking traces using SFT

The distilled models are SFT only: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B scores 28.9% on AIME 2024 just by copying R1's thinking.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner18

Thinking Mode

Qwen3 (Qwen Team, 2025), one model with two modes:

modelspost-training
Qwen3-235B-A22B, Qwen3-32Blong-CoT cold start → reasoning RL (GRPO) → thinking + non-thinking SFT → general RL
Qwen3-0.6B … 14Bstrong-to-weak distillation from the big ones, in both modes

◆ Thinking mode — the same weights either think first or answer right away, switched by the chat template.

For the small models, distillation beat running RL on them directly. Our 0.6B model learned to think by copying a bigger one (Friday's distillation).

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner19

Thinking Mode in Qwen3-0.6B

Back to our 100 GSM8K problems, same weights, now with thinking mode on:

Thinking first goes from 64% to 81%, and it writes 1,696 tokens a problem instead of 264.

Reasoning Models · Training a Reasoner20

The Think Block

enable_thinking=False in irishQwen's chat_prompt does nothing clever: it pre-fills an empty block.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen21

A Thinking Trace

It says "Wait" three times, re-reads the problem and checks its answer three times. Across all 100 problems it said "Wait" 617 times.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen22

Budget Forcing

◆ Budget forcing — once the think block reaches B tokens, force </think> so the model has to answer (Muennighoff et al., 2025, who also add "Wait" to make it think longer: 50% → 57% on AIME 2024).

In irishQwen it's one if-statement in pick_next_token.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen23

Test-Time Compute

◆ Test-time compute — computation spent while answering, instead of in training.

Even B = 0 gets 59%: cut off, it just works the problem in its answer instead (256 tokens on average). Only 100 problems, so it's bumpy, but the trend is up.

Same shape as the reasoning effort chart we started with: an effort setting works like a thinking budget, and the last tokens buy the least.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen24

Thinking Longer vs. Self-Consistency

The same tokens, spent two ways. Past a few hundred tokens thinking longer beat self-consistency: 77% vs 71% at about 1,100 tokens, 81% vs 76% at about 2,000.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen25

Train-Time and Test-Time Compute

OpenAI's o1 (September 2024): accuracy keeps improving with more RL (train-time compute) and with more time spent thinking (test-time compute).

AIME 2024one answerconsensus of 64
GPT-4o9.3%13.4%
o174.4%83.3%

Two knobs instead of one: a bigger model, or the same model thinking for longer.

Reasoning Models · Thinking in irishQwen26

The Cost of Thinking

Qwen3-0.6B, 100 problemsrighttokens per problemon our T4
answer right away464 s
show the steps6426495 s
think first811,69632 min

Every token is a full forward pass, so thinking costs about 6× the tokens of showing the steps, and you pay for it on every question, easy or not.

This is why reasoning APIs bill for thinking tokens, and why "how hard should it think?" is a setting: the Effort menu we started with, where Ultra "consumes usage limits faster".

Reasoning Models · What It Costs27

Overthinking

Right answers thought 1,107 tokens on average, wrong ones 2,986. The 11 that hit the cap never finished thinking, so they never answered.

◆ Overthinking — long thinking that doesn't help: the 37 problems it got right 8 times in 8 without thinking still thought for 782 tokens on average.

Reasoning Models · What It Costs28

Faithfulness

◆ Faithfulness — whether the chain of thought shows what actually decided the answer (Chen et al., Anthropic, 2025).

The thinking is text the model was rewarded for producing, not a window into the weights. Useful, but read it with that in mind.
